display.purpose: Compressed caps printed on a closed sleeve (sign-in, empty shelf, waiting) and on a missing cover.

headline.purpose: The record title on the liner board; title case, balanced wrap.

wordmark.purpose: "Vinyl Shelf" in the header strip only.

body.purpose: Artist line under the record title; the sign-in lead sentence.

body-sm.purpose: Header controls, notices, sleeve copy, the leaned readout, liner notes (0.8125rem from 64rem).

label.purpose: Condensed caps for track positions, credit roles, the catalogue line and the More below cue; beside what they name, never as a kicker.

sticker.purpose: Bold condensed caps on a hype sticker.

shadows.name: photo
shadows.purpose: Sleeve-sized objects on the studio ground: the open gatefold, the closed sleeve, the hype sticker.

shadows.name: disc
shadows.purpose: Every disc; separates each crescent in the stack.

shadows.name: crease
shadows.purpose: The fold where the liner board meets the cover panel (wide screens only).

motion.name: lean
motion.purpose: A disc sliding out of the stack on hover or focus (x -36% wide, y 28% phones); the open record sits at x -10% / y 8%.

motion.name: fold
motion.purpose: The liner board folding shut on its crease and reopening (rotateY 0 to -180deg from the left edge wide; rotateX 0 to 180deg from the top edge on phones); crossfade under reduced motion.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Hype sticker hover (scale 1.05, rotate -4deg from -8deg) and press (scale 0.97).

motion.name: tick
motion.purpose: The import count springing up to each new value; real number shown directly under reduced motion.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Transform animations jump to their end state; opacity still animates; the gatefold crossfades instead of folding.

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.purpose: Stack stands beside the gatefold as a column; app becomes viewport height.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.purpose: Liner notes split into tracklist and credits columns; sign-in shows the fanned discs.

rasterProvenance.method: Procedural, seeded (mulberry32, seed 0x5eedd15c), rendered in Playwright Chrome; no image model, nothing traced.

openDecisions: Board colour sourcing: client sampling is blocked by Discogs CORS, so carbon is the effective board; server-side sampling would need a contract change.
Discogs attribution placement count: currently one credit on the board and one over the stack.

narrative.overview:
A studio product shot of a record collection. The ground is a studio-white seamless sweep with soft photographic shadows; on it, one gatefold lies open at full size (the cover square on one panel, the liner notes printed on the inner board on the other, a crease between them) and the rest of the collection is fanned beside it as discs in their real colourways, each overlapping the next and showing a crescent. One record at a time gets the whole sleeve. The rest wait as a stack you can thumb through.

Type is set like liner notes: one variable family (Archivo) carrying the hierarchy through its width axis, condensed capitals for roles, positions and credit lines, regular weight for names and titles, hairline-ruled columns. Colour is almost all neutral; the only chromatic colours come from the records (cover art and named colourways) and from one sticker red that marks actions. Motion is physical: discs lean out of the stack on springs, and choosing one folds the board shut on its crease and opens it again on the new record.

Truth comes before decoration. A colourway is drawn only when Discogs names it; an unnamed record is drawn black and nothing is printed about its colour. Discogs data never appears without its credit.
keyCharacteristics: Studio-white ground, soft photographic drop shadows, no hard edges of light.
One open gatefold per screen; everything else is a fanned disc stack.
Two shapes only: squares (sleeves, boards, covers) and circles (discs, stickers).
Archivo Variable throughout; width (wdth 62 to 100) does the work other systems give to a second family.
Sticker red is the single signal colour; actions are round hype stickers or underlined text.
Springs only, transform and opacity only; reduced motion turns the fold into a crossfade.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Sticker Red marks actions and focus only: hype stickers, the focus ring, the caret, import progress. It is never a decoration, a heading colour or a background panel.

rules.name: The Carbon Board Rule
rules.body: The liner board is carbon unless the featured cover is CORS-readable, in which case it is printed in the cover's dominant colour deepened to 90%, with black (#141414) or white text chosen by computed contrast. Treat carbon as the effective default and sampling as a latent path. Where board colour is sourced from (client sampling, server-side sampling with a contract change, or carbon only) is an open decision with the user; do not settle it in a surface.

rules.name: The Named Colourway Rule
rules.body: Only a colourway Discogs names is drawn or printed ("2019 · Blue Marbled vinyl"). No name means a Lacquer Black disc and no colour claim in the text. Never guess a colour from the cover.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Archivo Variable is the only face. Hierarchy comes from the width axis (62 sleeve titles and wordmark, 72 labels, 78 headlines, 100 reading text) and weight, never from a second family or a system display face.

rules.name: The Liner Notes Rule
rules.body: Condensed caps label data the way a sleeve's credits do: in the left column of a term/value pair, as a track position, or as a credit line under the notes. They never float above a heading as a kicker or eyebrow.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Anything counted or timed (record counts, track durations, years, catalogue lines, the import counter) uses tabular numerals.

rules.name: The One Record Rule
rules.body: One record is open at full size; the rest of the collection is a stack. Never lay the collection out as a grid of equal square covers.

rules.name: The Clear Readout Rule
rules.body: Information about a leaned or hovered disc appears in the readout under the stack, never on top of a disc.

rules.name: The Product Shot Rule
rules.body: Shadows are soft, fall downward and belong to physical objects. No hard offset shadows, no glows, no shadows on text or on rules.

rules.name: The Two Shapes Rule
rules.body: If it is not a square of paper or a circle of vinyl or sticker, it has no shape at all: text actions, notices and controls sit directly on the ground without a container.

dos: **Do** keep one record open in the gatefold and the rest in the disc stack (The One Record Rule).
**Do** reserve Sticker Red for hype stickers, the focus ring, the caret and import progress (The One Signal Rule).
**Do** fall back to the Carbon Board with Studio White text whenever the cover cannot be sampled, and choose board text by computed contrast, never by assumption.
**Do** draw only the colourways Discogs names; draw an unnamed record in Lacquer Black and print nothing about its colour.
**Do** render the Discogs credit with every block of Discogs data.
**Do** set roles, positions and credit lines in condensed caps beside what they name, and names and titles in regular weight (The Liner Notes Rule).
**Do** animate with springs on `transform` and `opacity` only, and keep a crossfade path for reduced motion.
**Do** name a leaned disc in the readout under the stack, clear of the discs.
**Do** composite discs from the seeded raster plates; regenerate them with `scripts/disc-plates.ts`, never by tracing a real record.
donts: **Don't** use kicker or eyebrow labels above headings.
**Don't** use gradient text. (The fold crease and the notes fade are depth devices, not text treatments.)
**Don't** use hard offset shadows; every shadow is soft and photographic (The Product Shot Rule).
**Don't** make any other filled or rectangular button; actions are hype stickers or underlined text.
**Don't** introduce a second typeface or a system display face (The One Family Rule).
**Don't** lay the collection out as a grid of equal square covers.
**Don't** add rounded corners to paper; it is square, or it is a circle.
**Don't** show a stock image for a missing cover; print the title on the sleeve.
